instruction: Look up flights from Boston Logan Airport to Miami International Airport for tomorrow.

metadata.explanation: Variation uses same Delta.com website with different airport pair (BOS to MIA) for tomorrow. Reuses existing getter 'get_active_tab_html_parse' and metric 'check_direct_json_object' which parse Delta's flight search results HTML. Airport codes BOS and MIA are standard IATA codes. Task complexity remains identical to original.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic correctly verifies all instruction requirements: origin airport (BOS), destination airport (MIA), and date (tomorrow = Sun, Dec 22, 2025)

Data flow is semantically correct: getter extracts {time, start, end} from Delta.com flight search results HTML, expected.type='rule' causes get_rule() to return config['rules']={expected: {start, end, time}}, and metric extracts rules['expected'] to compare against getter result

The metric check_direct_json_object (line 420) correctly extracts expected_json=rules['expected'] which gives {start: 'BOS', end: 'MIA', time: 'Sun, Dec 22, 2025'} - this structure matches the getter output perfectly

Getter get_active_tab_html_parse can extract the needed state from Delta.com using class selectors: 'mach-flight-context-info__wrapper--date' for date, 'mach-flight-context-info__wrapper__info--separator' with child indices 0 and 1 for origin/destination airports
Expected values are semantically correct: BOS (Boston Logan Airport IATA code), MIA (Miami International Airport IATA code), and the correctly calculated tomorrow date in Delta.com's display format
No postconfig needed - the active tab should already show the flight search results after the user completes the task
The rule validator's error 'expected.type missing' is a structural warning about missing type field, but this does not affect semantic correctness - the evaluator will work correctly at runtime
